marketing_presentation.description: Identify shipping products, qualified configurations, prototypes and plans separately. Manufacturer interest and campaign targets are not signed agreements, verified adoption or sales.

CP/M remains commercially licensed. Non-exclusive implementation rights do not change software ownership or imply open-source licensing. Reference-code rights, certification scope and support terms must be stated before making firm offers.

Keep coprocessor implementation and integration details, unreleased next-generation-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries and revealing benchmarks confidential. Apply this embargo to presentations, questions, advertising, dealer scripts, sales proposals, OEM briefings, clinics and all attachments; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional display documentation may be shared. The released Apple II 6502 target and its June 1979 documentation may be demonstrated publicly.

Use released eight-bit software and explicitly identified qualified prototypes in demonstrations. Label prepared data and recordings, obtain partner clearance, and report measured resource and interoperability limits rather than implying universal performance.
Do not imply an engineering guarantee, product withdrawal date or promise that every model remains in production. Do not promise funded support for an unspecified duration.

Document common file formats and APIs. FlexiBUS and Logix video are optional; native displays, disks and conventional ports remain valid. Ordinary CP/M support does not guarantee every extended application, Z80 binary, file system or floppy format.

Publish electrical and transport rules, device-class profiles, host drivers, diagnostics and named qualification results. Other processors and operating systems may use their own drivers without adopting CP/M or Logix video. Device identification alone does not prove feature compatibility. Version 1 uses one device per point-to-point port, with no passive hub or daisy chain; its faster rate allows at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

Separate graphics API compatibility from controller cards, the digital monitor link and qualified display modes. FlexiBUS and the full Aurelia architecture are optional. An 80-column mode needs a qualified 640-pixel monitor; adding a card does not give existing 320-pixel launch monitors that resolution.

The NCC launch covers the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. The Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II are existing products presented alongside the three new interface/video cards. Cards initially use AION chips and include native Apple drivers and examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters as appropriate. Keep host requirements and supplier support explicit. AION C IDE 2.0 runs on Aurelia and cross-compiles native Apple II programs. Both video cards implement the full contemporary Aurelia TUI and graphics profile with ROM and libraries; S-100 TUI requires qualified CP/M extensions. The June 1979 release also targets native Apple II 6502 code, with Apple DOS 3.2-compatible output disks written on Aurelia through FlexiDisk II. Describe an optional Z80 coprocessor planned for qualified legacy applications. Availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model or hardware-dependent program. Keep its implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration confidential until the architecture reveal.
Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development. Publish a funded support duration before making a dated service promise.
Explain that eight-bit computers retain useful business roles while falling costs broaden home, education and personal use. There is no fixed date when all business customers switch platforms.

The current professional digital monitor interface cannot drive a consumer television. A computer intended to use an existing television requires separate display engineering; the basic-storage configuration remains unresolved.

after.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
after.objective: Demonstrate portable C applications and compatible peripherals and displays across computer brands, introduce the June 1979 Apple II/S-100 offerings, and recruit independent implementers through dated qualification and follow-up.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Build on Aurelia, run native code on Apple II, and retain familiar interaction with Logix video.
Independent software, peripherals and displays can adopt shared standards without adopting the whole Logix platform.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.

marketing_steps.description: Recruit independent computer, software and peripheral implementers.

marketing_presentation.description: Logix coordinates outreach, AION supports software and application integration, and DRI supports CP/M qualification. Prioritise North Star, with Lifeboat as a possible integration/distribution partner, then Vector Graphic. Both are strong CP/M prospects; FlexiBUS is a moderately strong fit, while Logix video is a moderate fit for North Star and a lower fit for Vector. Existing applications and display investment shape each proposal; outreach does not establish an agreement.

Cromemco is a moderate CP/M/FlexiBUS prospect but a weak Logix-video prospect because of its independent OS and graphics strategy. Altos is a moderately strong CP/M prospect with moderate FlexiBUS and limited video potential. Intertec has moderately strong CP/M and moderate host-specific FlexiBUS potential; schedule late-1979 evaluation and possible 1980 qualification. Heath/Heathkit is a moderate CP/M/FlexiBUS prospect for later feasibility work. Neither implies a June release or a host redesign.

Seek independent implementations in printers, disks, communications, input, instruments and specialist output. Match opportunities to vendor-owned product variants rather than relabelling every existing device. Printing needs explicit character/status and paper handling; plotting and specialist functions need their own profiles, while disks need geometry, durable writes, boot and recovery rules. Native faster disk interfaces remain valid.

marketing_steps.description: Publish separate compatibility profiles and update them for the June offerings.

marketing_presentation.description: Publish {cpm} host/CPU, memory and adapter requirements alongside DRI’s portable-extension release. Ordinary CP/M remains usable without TUI or FlexiBUS; extended services and application binaries require named supported configurations. Explain {tui} as shared interaction and {c} as source-level contracts with separate target builds. The Apple II/S-100 profiles and AION C 2.0 arrive at the June launch; later ERA and pointer capabilities are outside this release.

Publish {bus} electrical/transport rules, host drivers, device classes and diagnostics independently of CP/M and video. One device connects to each point-to-point port; passive hubs and daisy chains are unsupported, and the faster rate is at most {rate} KB/s before overhead. Distinguish the C display API, video controller and {video} monitor connection. Eighty columns require a qualified 640-pixel monitor; a consumer TV or existing 320-pixel monitor does not become compatible through a cable.

Provide {sdk}, published versions, reference-driver access, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. State non-exclusive own-brand implementation and component-access principles, supply priorities and manufacturer participation. Settle reference-code rights, CP/M licensing, support duration/staffing, maintenance funding, governance, certification scope, allocations and warranties before firm offers. Preserve each supplier’s ownership, branding and specialist support.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify the demonstrations, supplier contributions and public disclosure.

marketing_presentation.description: Rehearse named configurations with supplier workshops and record failures and corrections. Test the Aurelia/Model II document round trip separately from Aurelia compilation, FlexiDisk II Apple-format writing and Apple II execution. Measure memory/workspace, disk formats, loading/recalculation, UI redraw and peripheral behaviour; test ROM-bank restoration across display/disk calls. Book suitable space and audiovisual equipment, secure participant clearance and label prepared data or recordings.

Keep the Model II demonstration labelled prototype until its release. AION supplies the June cards; SMC is a future source subject to chip qualification. Apple’s participation concerns native Apple products, not S-100 endorsement. Separate shipping products, qualified demonstrations, prototypes and recruitment prospects; manufacturer interest, forecasts and targets are not sales or commitments.

Until {reveal}, describe the new architecture only as next-generation computers. Withhold product/processor/OS names, word size, ISA/registers, memory organization, clocks, performance figures, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology, future displays and coprocessor internals. Apply this to talks, Q&A, press, dealers, OEMs and attachments. Current CP/M/FlexiBUS/video documentation and the released Apple 6502 target are public. Answer architecture questions with the NCC 1980 disclosure plan; make no unspecified support-duration, withdrawal or engineering guarantee.

marketing_steps.description: Present cross-platform C development, familiar interfaces and the independent ecosystem.

marketing_presentation.description: The presentation lasts {programme_minutes} minutes, followed by questions. Show current products first and label the supplier roadmap separately.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Open with independent choice: shared application interfaces, documents and peripherals let customers keep useful work while changing computer brands. Introduce the software, bus and display standards as independently adoptable.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. DRI explains the portable CP/M extensions. Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the {model} prototype using separately qualified editions and an explicit transfer path. Show the {option} as a prototype; its recorded release is {release}, not the NCC date.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Feature {ledger} as an independent C-application pioneer. SSG demonstrates its native Z80 AION C implementation, ROM TUI forms and versioned balance exports to Abacus, explaining the benefit of shared editing and controls while retaining its accounting rules, ownership and support. This is General Ledger, not a larger accounting suite, a Model II port or a newly released Apple edition. Show how {basic} also uses shared TUI services without describing BASIC as a C port.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Operate a qualified FlexiBUS peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, supported class functions and driver requirements, attaching only with the port quiescent. Introduce the Apple II Expansion Card, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface and dual-format FlexiDisk II as separate choices.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Present {apple_video} and {s100_video} with ROM-backed TUI and callable libraries. On matching qualified monitors, demonstrate the full June 1979 Aurelia control behaviour and text/bitmap/sprite modes: frames, windows, editing, selection and redraw. Apple uses native 6502 code; S-100 TUI requires qualified CP/M/TUI extensions. Explain keyboard-command mappings and independent host performance. Preserve native Apple graphics/sound access; no automatic conversion of legacy graphics or later mouse/professional modes is implied.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Launch {compiler}: edit and compile a small shared C sample on Aurelia, save the native 6502 executable on an Apple DOS 3.2-compatible disk using {disk}, move the disk to Apple II and run it under its existing DOS installation. A compatible Disk II reader needs no Logix interface merely to read the disk; directly connecting FlexiDisk II to Apple does. Rebuild common TUI/drawing calls for Logix video, then show separately named native Apple graphics and speaker functions. The IDE stays on Aurelia; CPU-specific assembly and direct hardware access still need adapters. An Apple representative joins this native Apple demonstration without endorsing S-100 systems.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Give independent hardware pioneers a dedicated roadmap segment. Use {bridge} and {printer} to explain vendor-owned FlexiBUS bridge/native-interface approaches, and {leedex} and {sanyo} to explain purpose-built digital-input monitor variants. These are candidate paths in June, not shipping products or confirmed stage participants: the recorded estimated releases are {bridge_date}, {printer_date}, {leedex_date} and {sanyo_date}, respectively. Native Centronics printers remain behind a bridge; existing composite monitors do not become digital through a cable. Describe only tested raster/readability profiles, without promising 80 columns on every monitor. Invite supplier representatives only once participation and claims are cleared.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. {presenter} explains that shared C logic and documented APIs reduce migration work, while target-specific builds, data-format validation and testing remain necessary. Future computers will not execute Z80 binaries natively; describe the planned optional Z80 compatibility path without revealing its implementation. Continue CP/M tools and maintenance alongside future development; eight-bit systems retain business, home and education roles without a fixed replacement date.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Close with available products, prototype demonstrations and prospective supplier programmes clearly distinguished. Direct customers to dealer demonstrations and developers to the SDK, compatibility directory, migration clinics and implementation programme.

Publish named supported configurations, application editions, test failures and support contacts; distinguish shipping products, prototypes and qualification work.

Later printer and monitor candidates stay on the roadmap until their own dates and qualification evidence. Suppliers retain their own brands, licences, sales and support.

Track compatible-computer sell-through, qualified C and other application editions, peripheral shipments/classes, document interchange, support incidents, supplier concentration and component availability. Report progress and unresolved access/support issues, keeping future releases and NCC 1980 targets separate from results.
